themes_detail.label: Residential Noise Surge This Week
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints in residential areas spiked to 42 this week, a 95% increase from the 21.5-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden and significant quality-of-life disruption affecting Tottenville/Great Kills residents.
evidence: 42 residential noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 21.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.34)
95% spike represents statistically significant deviation from baseline
Most recent and acute spike in the entire dataset
reporting_angles: Canvass affected neighborhoods to identify noise source(s): construction, bars/venues, industrial activity, or events
Interview residents about sleep disruption and quality-of-life impact; identify whether complaints cluster geographically

themes_detail.label: Tree Planting Surge Signals Demand
themes_detail.summary: New Tree Request complaints surged 1900% this week to 5 complaints versus a 0.2 per-week baseline, indicating residents are urgently requesting street tree coverage—potentially revealing a long-standing gap in the district's canopy that aligns with the Community Board's repeated budget requests for forestry services.
evidence: 5 new tree requests THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (z-score: 10.97, highest anomaly in dataset)
Community Board has requested forestry services and street tree maintenance funding for multiple years without resolution
Damaged Tree complaints also rank 5th overall (430 over 90 days), indicating existing tree infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Map the tree request hotspots and interview residents about why NOW—are they responding to a new initiative, heat/flooding damage, or long-standing complaint fatigue?
Investigate unfunded forestry requests in Community Board budget submissions; report on backlog and timeline for tree maintenance/planting

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk and Building Infrastructure Deteriorating
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints doubled (103% spike to 17 this week vs. 8.4 baseline) and Building/Use complaints spiked 120% (25 last week vs. 11.4 baseline) over the prior 8 weeks, signaling accelerating physical infrastructure failures that may undermine pedestrian safety and property standards.
evidence: Sidewalk Condition: 17 complaints last week vs. 8.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.86, 103% spike)
Building/Use: 25 complaints last week vs. 11.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.38, 120% spike)
Flooring/Stairs: 5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 baseline (z-score: 3.58, 400% spike) suggests interior structural issues
Community Board has repeatedly requested street reconstruction funding from DOT—budget requests show unfunded need
reporting_angles: Document specific blocks with failed sidewalks, crumbling facades, and code violations; photograph and geo-map patterns
Interview DOT and building department about inspection backlogs and funding bottlenecks for repairs

themes_detail.label: Missing Street Signage Across District
themes_detail.summary: Street Sign - Missing complaints jumped 269% to 6 this week (3 weeks ago) versus a 1.6 per-week baseline, indicating gaps in wayfinding infrastructure that could compound navigation and safety concerns for residents and visitors.
evidence: 6 street sign complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.94, 269% spike)
Timing is 3 weeks old, making this less acute than current-week spikes but still statistically anomalous
May reflect weather damage (winter snow/ice, 4138 complaints over 90 days) or deferred maintenance
reporting_angles: Identify which streets are missing signs and whether pattern correlates with recent storms or construction
Check with DOT on sign replacement timelines and backlog

themes_detail.label: Stream Restoration Project at Critical Juncture
themes_detail.summary: The Arden Heights Woods Stream Restoration project (BMP AH-2) is in active public review at the City Planning Commission, offering a window for community input on environmental infrastructure that could address long-standing water system issues (631 complaints over 90 days) and align with the Community Board's sewer development requests.
evidence: Arden Heights Woods Stream Restoration in Public Review phase, heading to CPC Public Meeting - Vote
Community Board has made repeated capital budget requests for DEP sewer infrastructure development
Water System complaints (631 over 90 days) rank 4th in district, indicating systemic drainage/sanitation issues
reporting_angles: Report on what the stream restoration will accomplish and which neighborhoods benefit; include resident testimonials about flooding or water quality
Explain how this project relates to long-standing sewer infrastructure gaps the Community Board has flagged
